messages:
sophie (support): Hey team, ACME reports a bunch of 429s this morning but their console shows ~1.2M tokens remaining. Can someone help triage?
acme-corp-ops: Confirmed, 11:42-11:47 UTC we saw ~150 429s. Example request id: r-0a1b2c3d. We only started seeing it after a bulk ingestion job.
acme-corp-ops: Quick curl repro we ran: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \u005c
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' \u005c
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \u005c
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","input":"test"}'
```
acme-corp-ops: Header shows 429 and body: '{"error":"rate_limited","code":429,"quota_key":"acct:acme-prod"}'
sophie (support): Console screenshot attached by customer shows token counters and per-minute rate panel both green. They also shared this console link: https://console.redwood.example/tenants/acme/usage
derek (eng-sre): Thanks. First guess: visibility/aggregation lag vs enforcement window. Can you share exact request timestamps and any gateway logs?
acme-corp-ops: Pasted the gateway log snippet: ```
[2026-03-12T11:42:03Z] request_id=r-0a1b2c3d tenant=acme method=POST path=/v1/generate latency=54ms status=429
[2026-03-12T11:42:04Z] request_id=r-0a1b2c3e tenant=acme method=POST status=200
```
amce-typo: (edited) apologizing for noise - above is correct.
maria (eng-infra): I'll check the ingestion pipeline. Quick note: there was a small Kafka consumer lag spike in the quota-aggregator at 11:41:30 UTC for ~90s on node qa-02. Could be the aggregation window cutover.
josh (product): Customer-facing disparity. If enforcer is strict and console is showing post-aggregated counts, that's bad. We need repro steps and timeline to communicate.
derek (eng-sre): Can we confirm the aggregation window config? Are we using 60s sliding windows vs 1m fixed windows for this tenant? If aggregator delayed by 90s, console could show tokens after enforcer already consumed them.
quota-bot: [automated] tenant=acme snapshot: tokens_remaining=1,234,567 window=60s last_update=2026-03-12T11:43:55Z
amce-corp-ops: Customer also says they used a burst of parallel requests (x60) from a single API key at 11:42.
derek (eng-sre): Action items: 1) maria to check aggregator consumer offsets and commit times (possible reproc). 2) infra to attach enforcer logs correlating token counter reads for tenant=acme. 3) support to get customer request_ids for all 429s.
maria (eng-infra): Confirming consumer lag on qa-02 was due to GC pause on aggregator JVM (we're tracking via infra metrics). Offsets were committed ~75s later than message timestamps. That explains console showing counts after enforcement.
derek (eng-sre): Root cause hypothesis: aggregator commit lag -> console reflects late-committed aggregates -> enforcer enforces from real-time token store (correct) -> user sees 429s while console still shows tokens.
sophie (support): Ok will draft customer message explaining timing lag and workaround (reduce burst or request short backoff). Also asking infra for mitigation ETA.
josh (product): Can we add an explicit 'last_updated' tooltip on quota panels and surface ingestion lag? This will reduce confusion.
maria (eng-infra): Mitigation: increased heap, tuned GC flags on aggregator JVM, redeployed consumer group; Kafka lag cleared at 11:44:30 UTC. Longer-term: move aggregator to native process and add per-tenant commit tracing.
derek (eng-sre): Repro steps for eng: 1) start high-parallel load (>=50rps) for single tenant 2) pause aggregator consumer for 60-90s 3) observe enforcer 429s while console still shows tokens 4) resume consumer and see console catch up. Use tenant=acme test key rwd-test-001.
sophie (support): Customer update posted: "Thanks — reducing parallelism fixed it for now. We'll follow up if it recurs." :thumbsup:
acme-corp-ops: Thanks everyone. Please keep us posted on the infra follow-up and ETA.
maria (eng-infra): Filing infra ticket INFRA-2026-114: "Quota aggregator GC-caused lag -> visibility mismatch". ETA: perf patch + rollout in 48h.
derek (eng-sre): I'll add an internal postmortem link once written. For now marking as triaged. :white_check_mark:
